uncited: The rendering pipelines for 3D Gaussian Splatting originated from the need to render millions of Gaussian primitives in real-time, a task for which traditional triangle-based rasterizers are inefficient due to the soft, overlapping nature of the primitives.
The core algorithm was introduced in the seminal 3D Gaussian Splatting paper [2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md], which established the projection and alpha-compositing pipeline.

Subsequent extensions have adapted this pipeline for specific domains: volume rendering [6093-volume-encoding-gaussians.md], physical relighting [6227-brdf-and-relighting-extensions.md], and cross-platform deployment [17626-xpr-rendering-pipeline.md].
The pipeline's efficiency relies on the affine approximation of the perspective projection and tile-based sorting, which allows for parallel execution on GPUs.
